enade-2011-computing-q13.notes: REAL DEFECT FOUND. Statement's interval-scheduling pseudocode is genuinely split by a spurious figure-01.png asset inserted mid-algorithm. Inspected the rendered crop directly: it does not show any legitimate figure - it shows a large, wrongly-bounded region spanning unrelated content (Q11's alternatives D/E, all of Q12's full statement+alternatives, and part of Q13's own pseudocode continuation), i.e. a mis-cropped chunk of a completely different part of the page. Root cause not yet isolated to a specific fix (a region-detection bbox computation issue, distinct from the orphan-marker/column bugs already fixed this phase) - left undiagnosed and undocumented as code because a first attempt at a related fix (widening the orphan-marker exclusion in layout.py, tried while investigating a similar false-positive on Q22) was found to regress 2021's already-certified gold corpus and was reverted (see docs/decisions.md, Phase 2A ADR). Recorded here as a known, disclosed content-corruption defect requiring dedicated future investigation, not silently left unmarked. extraction_status should remain needs_review; the spurious asset should not be treated as trustworthy.

enade-2011-computing-q22.notes: REAL DEFECT FOUND. Truth-table reconstruction is missing its header row ("A B C D S") and the true first data row ("0 0 0 0 1") - confirmed against rendered page 14: the real table has a text header plus 16 data rows, but both the structured Markdown table AND its own mandatory visual-fallback crop (table-01.png) start from the second real row ("0 0 0 1 0") onward, 15 rows total. Root cause identified: the header's single-character cells ("A","B","C","D") are narrow enough to match layout.py's _ORPHAN_MARKER_RE (built for the circled A-E alternative-choice pictograph glyphs, ~17.5-20pt wide) even though they are plain ~7.2pt text glyphs, so they get merged into nonsense fragments ("A\tS", "C\t0", etc.) that then fall outside detect_tables()'s row/column geometry, dropping both the header and the real first row from the detected region entirely (not just from the rendered table - from the region bounding box itself, so even the 'mandatory visual fallback' safety net is incomplete for this specific table). A width-based fix was implemented and verified to solve this case, but was reverted after confirming (via full 2021 byte-diff) that it also changes three already-certified 2021 gold files (Q23, Q34, D4), each of which merges a similarly narrow diagram-label letter through the same code path - PROMPT Phase 2A section 24 forbids that without an explicit, visually-revalidated schema migration, which this was not. Recorded as a known, disclosed structural defect for a future, more targeted fix (e.g. scoping the fix to detect_tables()'s own header-row recovery rather than the shared orphan-marker mechanism). extraction_status should remain needs_review; content_blocks' TableBlock must not be promoted to validated.

enade-2011-computing-q23.notes: REAL DEFECT FOUND. Statement and alternative D/E text are missing inline mathematical notation that appears inline in the real PDF (confirmed on rendered page 14): the alphabet symbol "Σ = {a,b,c}", the empty-string symbol "λ", and (in alternative E) the full regular expression "(a+b+c)*(ab)*abc(a+b+c)*" are all absent from the extracted text, leaving grammatically broken sentences ("...que" trailing into the figure with no continuation; "...a linguagem sobre em que..."; "...expressao regular ."). The automaton diagram and the grammar-rules block (figure-01.png/figure-02.png) are both correctly captured as complete, uncropped image assets - this is specifically about small inline math notation that is not being recognized as figure content and is not extracting as text either (a different, apparently font/rendering-based defect from D3's monospace pseudocode arrow glyph, not yet root-caused - most likely these specific symbols are set via a dedicated math/formula sub-font or inline image PyMuPDF's text layer does not expose the way it does the alternative-marker pictograph font). Not attempted this phase given the risk profile already demonstrated by the Q22 investigation and the volume of remaining Phase 2A work; recorded as a disclosed, real content-loss defect requiring its own dedicated investigation. extraction_status should remain needs_review.
